constitution.history: several previous (dating to 1684); latest entered into force 8 June 1968 (Bermuda Constitution Order 1968)
constitution.amend: proposal procedure - NA; passage by an Order in Council in the UK

courts.highest: Court of Appeal (consists of the court president and at least 2 justices); Supreme Court (consists of the chief justice, 4 puisne judges, and 1 associate justice); the Judicial Committee of the Privy Council (in London) is the court of final appeal
courts.judges: Court of Appeal justice appointed by the governor; justice tenure by individual appointment; Supreme Court judges nominated by the Judicial and Legal Services Commission and appointed by the governor; judge tenure based on terms of appointment

citizenship.descent: at least one parent must be a citizen of the UK

world: has not submitted an ICJ jurisdiction declaration; non-party state to the ICCt

gov.type: Overseas Territory of the UK with limited self-government; parliamentary democracy

executive.chosen: the monarchy is hereditary; governor appointed by the monarch; following legislative elections, the governor usually appoints the leader of the majority party or majority coalition as the premier
executive.cabinet: Cabinet nominated by the premier, approved by the governor

b: Bermuda is a separate legal jurisdiction to the United Kingdom and has its own laws.
There are no nude or topless beaches, and it is illegal for anyone to be topless in public.
Do not become involved with drugs of any kind. Penalties for possessing or importing drugs include prison sentences of up to 25 years and heavy fines.
It is illegal to drink alcohol in public outside of licensed premises.

There are severe penalties for breaking weapons laws.
Same-sex relationships are legal in Bermuda.
Bermuda allows same-sex domestic partnerships. Following a change in the law, same-sex partners can no longer marry – marriages before 14 March 2022 remain valid.
Public attitudes are tolerant but conservative. Some people may not approve of same-sex couples showing affection in public.
